title: Ledger cap checker CLI (P14 larger benchmark)

content.audience: Synthetic benchmark operator measuring the studio's build path at a larger, multi-module scale
content.problem_statement: Measure whether the bounded builder and independent reviewer can deliver a multi-module Python standard-library CLI with an internal module API (parser, rules engine, report writer) that validates a spending ledger read from stdin and reports category totals against caps, judged by frozen exact-output cases with held-out edge cases and a separate extended held-out suite. Larger here means more interacting requirements and modules, not line count. Synthetic benchmark, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Category totals
steps: Pipe a ledger into the CLI with no arguments
Read each category total and the grand total

user_flows.name: Caps
steps: Run with one or more --cap name=amount
Read ok or over per capped category
Check exit status 4 when any is over

user_flows.name: Month filter
steps: Read totals for that month only

user_flows.name: Invalid rows
steps: Pipe a ledger with bad rows
Read every bad line number and reason

user_flows.name: Invalid arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read invalid input and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only. Entry point src/main.py plus a package src/ledger with at least three modules: parse.py (row parsing and validation), rules.py (totals and caps) and report.py (text and JSON output). main.py only parses arguments and wires the modules together
Runtime rule: QA runs python3 -I src/main.py from the product root, so src is not on the import path. main.py must insert its own directory into sys.path before importing ledger

stdin is a ledger split into lines on newline; one trailing carriage return per line is removed. Lines are numbered from 1, counting every line. A line that is empty or only whitespace, or that starts with #, is skipped

Every other line has exactly three comma-separated fields date,category,amount with no trimming. date is a real calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. category is 1 to 20 of a-z, 0-9 or underscore. amount matches -?digits with an optional . and 1 or 2 digits
A row's reason is the first that applies in this order: bad field count, bad date, bad category, bad amount. All lines are validated even when --month is given
If any row is invalid, print one line per invalid row in line order as: line N: reason, print nothing else and exit 1
Otherwise total each category in integer cents. Money is printed as optional minus sign, whole part, dot, two digits (for example -0.05, 3.10, 1200.00); zero is 0.00

Text report: one line per category in ascending category order, then a final line total T where T is the sum of the printed category totals. An uncapped category line is: name total. A capped one is: name total / cap status, where status is over when total is greater than cap, else ok

--cap name=amount (repeatable, at most 5, each name once) caps a category. name follows the category rule; amount uses the amount rule without a minus sign. A capped category with no rows is still listed with total 0.00
--month YYYY-MM (a real month, at most once) keeps only rows whose date is in that month before totalling

--format text or json (at most once, default text). JSON is json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True) plus newline, where report is {categories: [{name, total, cap, status}], total}; money values are strings in the money format, and cap and status are null when uncapped
Any other argument, a flag without its value, or an invalid or repeated value prints exactly: invalid input, then newline, and exits 2, before reading rows
Exit 4 when the report has at least one over category, else exit 0. No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

data_contracts.name: ledgercheck/1
data_contracts.description: Synthetic CSV-like ledger lines on stdin; text or one JSON line on stdout

acceptance_checks.statement: With no arguments print each category total in category order, then the grand total
--cap marks each capped category ok or over and exits 4 when any is over
acceptance_checks.measure: Exact stdout and exit code 4 when over, else 0

acceptance_checks.statement: --format json prints the same report as one JSON line
--month YYYY-MM totals only rows dated in that month
Invalid rows are all reported by line number and reason, with exit 1 and no report

cases.stdout:
line 1: bad date
line 2: bad category
line 3: bad field count
line 4: bad amount

acceptance_checks.statement: Invalid arguments print invalid input and exit 2

risks.risk: The 10-case build limit cannot hold the whole larger suite
risks.mitigation: A separate frozen extended held-out suite is scored after the build on the exported package

risks.risk: The builder imports sibling modules without fixing sys.path under python3 -I
risks.mitigation: The runtime rule is part of the frozen scope; QA would fail every case otherwise

risks.risk: Held-out cases leak to the builder
risks.mitigation: The studio hides held-out cases; the repository copy is never sent to runtime roles

obligations: Keep this frozen version unchanged; changes need a new benchmark version
maintenance.review_interval: On recipe, role prompt, route or model change

tasks.title: Implement the multi-module ledger cap checker
tasks.deliverable: src/main.py and the src/ledger package that pass every acceptance check
